commitResults.messageTitle: A-Assertions: Add assertions to document code assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Several places in the code rely on assumptions that should always hold
if the surrounding code is correct, but nothing states or checks them.
For example, TaskList.get and TaskList.remove are only ever called with
an index that Percy has already validated, and Parser only constructs a
Task once it has confirmed the description and dates are present.

Make these assumptions explicit with the assert feature so that a broken
assumption fails loudly and close to its cause during development,
instead of surfacing later as a confusing NullPointerException or
IndexOutOfBoundsException:

* constructors (Task, Deadline, Event, Storage, Percy) assert that their
  reference arguments are non-null
* TaskList.get / remove assert the index is in range; add asserts the
  task is non-null; the seeded constructor asserts the list is non-null
* Parser asserts its input is non-null and that, once validation has
  passed, a deadline/event string has split into the expected number of
  parts
* Percy.resolveIndex asserts its return value is a valid index

Assertions are disabled by default at run time, so enable them for the
`run` task by adding -ea to applicationDefaultJvmArgs. Gradle already
runs tests with assertions enabled, so the existing test suite now also
exercises these checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-CodeQuality: Refactor for readability and less duplication
commitResults.messageBody:
A pass over the code looking for duplication, magic literals and methods
that mixed levels of abstraction.

Parser
 * extract parseDate(), removing three near-identical try/catch blocks
   around LocalDate.parse and two copies of the "yyyy-mm-dd" message
 * pull the " /by ", " /from " and " /to " markers into named constants
   and rename fromParts/toParts to descriptionAndDates/startAndEnd
 * rename toType to toCommandType and use a switch expression

Ui
 * the eight show* methods were built from four repeated fragments;
   extract showNumberedTasks(), showTaskChange() and showTaskDetail() so
   each public method is a single call

Task / Storage
 * replace markDone()/unmarkDone() with setDone(boolean); this also
   removes an "if (isDone)" branch in Storage.parseLine
 * define the save-file field separator once (Task.FILE_SEPARATOR) and
   use it on both the reading and writing side, replacing the magic
   " \| " split pattern and the scattered " | " literals
 * turn the if/else-if type dispatch in parseLine into a switch

Percy
 * the MARK and UNMARK branches differed only by a boolean and the
   confirmation message; extract setDoneStatus(arguments, done)

MainWindow
 * name the window-close delay (EXIT_DELAY) instead of a bare 1.2

No behavioural change: the save-file format is unchanged and the build
plus all 30 tests pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Streams: Replace element-by-element loops with streams
commitResults.messageBody:
The collection-processing loops in Storage and TaskList each built up a
result by mutating a local list; a stream pipeline states the same
intent (map, filter, collect) more directly.

* TaskList: add stream() exposing the tasks as a Stream<Task>, and
  reimplement find() as stream().filter(...).collect(...)
* Storage.load: read the file with Files.readAllLines and pipe the
  lines through map(parseLine).filter(nonNull).collect(...). This also
  removes the BufferedReader/FileReader plumbing and the manual
  readLine loop
* Storage.save: build the file contents with
  stream().map(Task::toFileFormat).collect(joining) instead of an
  index-based for loop

No behavioural change: the save-file format is byte-for-byte the same
and the build plus all tests (now 31) pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: C-Update: Add an update command to edit a task in place
commitResults.messageBody:
Until now the only way to fix a mistake in a task was to delete it and
add it again, which loses its done status and its position in the list.

Add an `update` command that changes just the fields you name:

    update <number> [new description] [/by <date>] [/from <date>] [/to <date>]

e.g. `update 2 /by 2019-12-01` moves a deadline without touching its
description, and `update 3 /to 2020-06-30` changes only an event's end
date. At least one field must be given, and a date field is rejected if
it does not apply to that task's type (checked before anything is
changed, so a rejected update leaves the task untouched).

* Task/Deadline/Event: fields are mutable again, with setDescription,
  setBy, setFrom, setTo (and getBy/getFrom/getTo) guarded by the same
  non-null assertions as the constructors
* Parser: UPDATE command type and parseUpdate(), returning an UpdateSpec
  whose null fields mean "leave unchanged"
* Percy.applyUpdate: validates the request, mutates the existing task,
  saves, and reports it via Ui.showUpdated
* Tests: parseUpdate parsing/validation and the new setters

commitResults.messageTitle: A-BetterGui: Highlight error replies in the chat window
commitResults.messageBody:
All of Percy's replies looked the same, so a rejected command (a typo,
a bad date, an out-of-range task number) blended into the ordinary
conversation instead of standing out as something to fix.

  error, via wasLastResponseError()

doesn't exist." in a red bubble instead of the default grey one.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle JavaFX natives for every platform in the shadow jar
commitResults.messageBody:
percy.jar failed to start on Windows with "Error initializing
QuantumRenderer: no suitable pipeline found" / "No toolkit found".
Cause: the javafx {} block only bundles native graphics libraries for
whichever OS builds the jar, so a jar built on this Mac only contained
macOS natives (.dylib) - no Windows .dll or Linux .so was present, so
JavaFX couldn't initialize any rendering pipeline at all on those OSes.

Add explicit javafx-base/graphics/controls/fxml dependencies for win,
mac, mac-aarch64, linux and linux-aarch64 (23.0.2), on top of the
existing javafx {} block. JavaFX's NativeLibLoader picks the native
library matching the current OS/arch at startup, so it's safe to have
every platform's binaries on the classpath at once - one jar now runs
on all five.

Verified: ./gradlew clean shadowJar build still passes all 69 tests
and runs correctly on this Mac (jar grew 8.5MB -> 10.8MB); the jar now
contains prism_d3d.dll/glass.dll (+ the MSVC redistributable DLLs, so
Windows doesn't need one installed separately), libglass.so/libglassgtk3.so
(Linux), and the existing .dylib files (Mac).
